topic: Art, Crafts & Culture of Andhra Pradesh

items.front: AP's classical dance, its village of origin and 17th-c. codifier?
items.back: Kuchipudi; from Kuchipudi village (Krishna dist.); codified by Siddhendra Yogi (composed Bhamakalapam).
Kuchipudi emphasises graceful lasya (feminine); Kathakali/Yakshagana are tandava (vigorous). It is a recognised classical form.

items.front: Ritual 'dance of warriors' revived from the Kakatiya era?
AP ritual dance honouring Shiva (Veerabhadra); two drum-based folk dances?
items.back: Veeranatyam; Dappu and Tappeta Gullu (shepherds' dances).

items.front: Ballad-narration folk form of AP (with tambura), from Jangam Katha?
Kalamkari — its two AP centres and their techniques?
items.back: Srikalahasti (free-hand pen) and Machilipatnam/Pedana (block-print); a hand-painted cotton textile (GI).

items.front: AP's two famous wooden toy crafts and their woods?
items.back: Kondapalli toys (Punki/Tella Poniki wood, Krishna dist.) and Etikoppaka lac-turned toys (Ankudu wood, Visakhapatnam; GI).

items.front: String-instrument craft (GI) of the Vizianagaram region?

items.back: Dharmavaram (silk), Venkatagiri, Uppada Jamdani, Mangalagiri (and Pochampally ikat).

items.front: Brass craft of Srikakulam and the stone-carving craft of Palnadu (GI)?
AP's four-day harvest festival and the Telugu New Year?
items.back: Makara Sankranti (Bhogi–Sankranti–Kanuma–Mukkanuma); Ugadi is the Telugu New Year.

items.front: The Telugu Kavitrayam and the joint work they created?
items.back: Nannaya, Tikkana and Errana — the Telugu Mahabharatam; Nannaya is the 'Adikavi'.

items.front: Amaravati school & Nagarjunakonda — their signature Buddhist feature?
items.back: White-limestone narrative reliefs and the tall carved ayaka pillars (Satavahana–Ikshvaku patronage).
Ponduru handspun Khadi (Srikakulam) got a GI tag (Dec 2025); Nandamuri Balakrishna received a Padma Bhushan 2025 (Art).
